question: Who was the Governor - General of India when Doctrine of Lapse was introduced in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Dalhousie.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Doctrine of Lapse** was introduced by **Lord Dalhousie,** who was the **Governor-General of India **from **1848 to 1856.**
 
• The doctrine allowed the **British East India Company** to **take over the territories **of Indian rulers who died without a** male heir.**
 
• Lord Dalhousie implemented this policy in order to** expand British control **over India and to **eliminate **the local rulers who were seen as **obstacles to British rule.**
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse was highly **controversial** and led to widespread **resentment **among Indian rulers and their subjects.
 
• **Lord Mountbatten** was the **last British Governor-General of India,** who oversaw the transfer of power to India in **1947**.
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** was the **Governor-General of Bengal ,** who served from **1786 to 1793.**
 
• **Lord Canning** was the Governor-General of India during the **Indian Rebellion of 1857.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Mountbatten **was appointed as the** Governor-General of India in 1947**, and he played a key role in the **transfer of power** from the **British to the Indian government.**
 
• **Lord Cornwallis** was a **British military commander** who served as the Governor-General of India during a period of significant **British expansion** in India. 
 
 
• He is also known for his role in the** American War of Independence.**
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning** was the Governor-General of India during the Indian Rebellion of **1857**, which was a major uprising against British rule in India. 
 
 
• He is remembered for his efforts to **restore peace and order **in the aftermath of the rebellion.
 
 
 
• Hence, the** correct answer** is option 2, Lord Dalhousie.
